name: Classic Chicken Cacciatore (Braised)

fit.reason: 495 cal is within 400-650; 15g carb is <=35g; scalable braise; budget meal-prep; not a seafood dish.

dupe_check.catalog: NOT a dupe of slow-cooker-chicken-cacciatore-pasta (that is a slow-cooker PASTA dish: chicken breast + penne + jarred pasta sauce, high-carb). This is the classic low-carb braise: bone-in thighs/drumsticks simmered in tomato-wine sauce with mushrooms/peppers/olives, no pasta or rice. Only 1 of 4 axes (Italian tomato flavor family) overlaps; protein cut, method, and starch all differ.
dupe_check.pool: No other cacciatore or Italian tomato-braised chicken among accepted-slugs read fresh; french-chicken-fricassee (cream/white-wine) and chicken-marsala-skillet (marsala, no tomato) are distinct.

seafood_note: Recipe lists 3 optional anchovy fillets as an omittable umami booster (already flagged unmapped). The dish is a chicken braise, not seafood; anchovy can be dropped at spec. Flagging for decider awareness.
cross_protein_collisions: Structurally this is an Italian tomato-wine braise with peppers/mushrooms/olives. Watch for a same-dish twin in other proteins: a turkey-thigh cacciatore, a pork or sausage cacciatore, or a 'hunter-style' braised turkey/pork with the same tomato-wine + olive + pepper profile would be the same dinner with a swapped protein. Decider should cross-check turkey/pork pools for any cacciatore / 'hunter's' / 'chasseur' braise.
